subject.title: fix: provider timeoutSeconds does not raise the LLM stream watchdog ceiling

question: Should OpenClaw honor an existing provider `timeoutSeconds` setting as the stream-watchdog ceiling even when a provider plugin rebuilds the resolved model, accepting the resulting longer but still bounded silent-stream window?
rationale: The implementation is a targeted repair of an existing documented setting, but it intentionally changes when affected existing runs are aborted; that availability trade-off cannot be resolved from source correctness alone.

options.title: Accept the documented timeout contract
options.body: Merge the patch so explicitly configured provider timeouts consistently bound both transport and stream-watchdog behavior after plugin normalization.

options.title: Pause for a narrower policy
options.body: Hold the PR while maintainers define whether plugin-rebuilt models should retain this host-owned timeout or require an explicit compatibility boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the documented timeout contract
recommendation.body: Merge the patch so explicitly configured provider timeouts consistently bound both transport and stream-watchdog behavior after plugin normalization.
